_doc: Sects the player can join. welcome (SECT-032, optional per sect): what the steward gives a new disciple who reports at the sect's home hall {line (non-empty, <= 160 chars, {player} is replaced), items {item_id: count}: 1-2 kinds, 1-5 each, total shop price <= 60}. Optional home_region (TRAV-004, a region id): where the sect lives; older saves are credited with having visited it. Alignment bounds are inclusive. min_realm is a realm id. cultivation_bonus multiplies qi gathering for members. Ranks are ascending; each rank has name and contribution (lifetime contribution needed; the first rank needs 0) plus optional (G-011): min_realm (realm id needed for the rank), min_stage (SECT-004, optional int, default 0: a stage index within min_realm that the disciple must also have reached; ignored without min_realm), trial (enemy id from enemies.json; promotion to that rank needs winning a sparring match against it, which never kills, robs or loots; not allowed on the first rank), stipend ({spirit_stones, items: {item_id: count}} paid at the end of each month while you hold the rank) and monthly_duty (contribution to earn each month; falling short withholds that month's stipend, never demotes; waived the month you are promoted). Promotion to a rank without a trial is automatic once its contribution and min_realm are met. robe_color (optional, hex) is the robe members wear on the world map. court_drill (GFX-241, optional): {count 2-6, form sword|fist|ledger}, disciples drilling on the sect hall court in its home region (none in rain, storm or fog). shop (optional, G-008c): contribution shop entries [{item_id, contribution (cost, >= 1), min_rank (rank index needed, default 0)}]; spending contribution never lowers rank (rank follows lifetime contribution). A shop breakthrough pill (effects.breakthrough_realm R) must sit at a min_rank whose min_realm is below R, so a member can claim the pill that helps them reach R before they have reached it. reputation (top level): standing with each sect, separate from alignment; start value, min/max range, leave_penalty (lost with a sect when you leave it), mission_rate (reputation per point of mission contribution with your own sect), tiers [{min, name, price_mult}] ascending by min (price_mult applies at merchants whose region place has that sect as 'faction'). Per-sect reputation: min_join (reputation needed to join) and deed_scale (a witnessed alignment change of D moves this sect's reputation by D * deed_scale; negative = the sect admires what others condemn). Effects can also change reputation directly with {"reputation": {sect_id: delta}}. contest (SECT-038, optional per sect): the yearly outer-sect contest {month (1-12, the calendar month it is open), rounds (2-3), foes [enemy ids from enemies.json, weakest first, one per round], prizes [{contribution >= 0, spirit_stones >= 0}] one per round won, power_mults (SECT-043, optional) [one float 0.4-2.0 per foe, default 1.0, scaling that round's foe on top of the enemy's own power_mult]; one entry per calendar year even after leaving and rejoining (character last_contest_year)}; a reported disciple of rank <= 1 may enter at the home hall once per year, fighting never-lethal bouts in order until a loss. lecture (SECT-005, optional per sect): the elder's monthly lecture {name, elder (C-270, optional text for {elder}, default "the elder"), topic (optional text for {topic}, default "the lesson"), lines (optional array of non-empty strings, scenes shown instead of "You attend <name>"; {elder} and {topic} are filled in; line month index % size is used so each month reads differently), days (>= 1, time it takes), qi_days (>= 0, days of qi gathered at the hall's density), insight_chance (0..1, plus 0.005 per Comprehension point above 10), insights [dao insight ids from dao.json; the first not yet known may be glimpsed]}; once per calendar month per disciple (sect.lecture_month). factions (top level, LW-002, optional): sects as living factions (SectFactions). strength_base: a sect's strength is the sum over its living NPC members of strength_base ^ realm index (mortal 1, Qi Refining base, Foundation base^2...). recruit: each month each sect, with monthly_chance (0..1), takes in one rogue generated NPC who cultivates, is min_age_years..max_age_years old, is not the player's spouse or descendant, and whom the sect would accept (alignment, realm). clash (LW-002b): each month each righteous/demonic sect pair (sect `alignment` tags; neutral sects never clash) clashes with monthly_chance (0..1); the loser (chosen by relative strength) loses `casualties` (>= 1) living NPC members; a clash involving the player's sect sets the world flag sect_call_<sect id>, unlocking that sect's call mission. trial_lessons (SECT-046): each lost promotion trial for the rank you are trying for lowers that examiner's power by per_loss, up to max; reset when you are promoted.

sects.name: Azure Cloud Sect

welcome.line: Welcome to Azure Cloud, {player}. Your name is on the roll; take these, and ask the elders when you are lost.

sects.description: An orthodox sect on misty peaks. Values virtue, discipline and the protection of mortals.

lecture.name: Elder Feng's sword lecture
lines: {elder} sets a leaf on still water and has you cut it without a ripple; the lesson is {topic} held in a quiet hand.
{elder} says a stance is only a sentence, and intent is the one who speaks it. You spend the morning learning to mean what you cut.
{elder} walks the line of disciples and taps each elbow with a bamboo rod. "Too proud. Lower it. {topic} bends before it breaks."
{elder} draws once, and the hall's lamps all lean toward the blade. No one is told to watch; everyone does.
{elder} teaches the first stance by refusing to teach it, until you stop reaching for it and it arrives.
{elder} has you drill the same thrust until your arm forgets it is yours. "Now," says {elder}, "it is {topic}, not you."
{elder} speaks of an old rival who never once lost a duel and never once won a fight, and lets you work out the difference.
{elder} sheathes a bare blade slowly. "The best of {topic} ends before it is drawn." Half the hall pretends to understand.
{elder} cuts a falling petal in three and says that a calm breath is the real edge of {topic}.

sects.name: Blood Lotus Sect

welcome.line: {player}. The Lotus does not coddle. Here: one pill and a salve. Whether you need them is the first test.

sects.description: A feared demonic sect. Strength is the only law; the weak are resources.

lecture.name: the Blood Elder's slaughter sermon
lines: {elder} speaks of hunger as the oldest teacher; by the end of the sermon your own pulse sounds loud in your ears.
{elder} lays a cracked skull on the altar and asks what is left when {topic} is finished. No one answers. {elder} smiles anyway.
{elder} says the weak are only unspent qi walking about. The hall is very quiet while the sermon's meaning sinks in.
{elder} teaches that every breath taken is a breath owed, and that {topic} is merely collecting.
{elder} paces between the braziers, voice rising and falling like a tide of blood, and you find you are nodding along.
{elder} makes each disciple name the last life they took, then tells them to take the next one with better manners.
{elder} calls pity a rust that eats the blade, and the sermon on {topic} grows warm, red and very patient.
{elder} speaks in a low voice of the sea of blood beneath the sect, and of what it asks of those who drink from it.
{elder} says the Dao of {topic} is honest: it never promises mercy, only an ending. Many of the disciples find that comforting.

sects.name: Myriad Treasure Pavilion

welcome.line: {player}, entered in the ledger. A pill and some paper on account; the Pavilion collects on everything, eventually.

sects.description: A merchant sect that trades with anyone who pays. Rewards craftsmen generously.

lecture.name: the Chief Steward's ledger lesson
lines: {elder} opens a ledger and shows that qi is simply coin that breathes: what you take in must be balanced by what you give out.
{elder} teaches the weighing of a bargain by letting you lose a small one on purpose, then explains the loss line by line.
{elder} says a good cultivator and a good merchant both know the price of patience. Your abacus beads click in agreement.
{elder} draws a column of figures on the board and has you find the single lie hidden in it. {topic} never forgives a rounded sum.
{elder} tells of a rival house that sold its own roof to buy a pill, and asks what the pill was really worth.
{elder} lectures on credit, trust and the long breath of trade: qi borrowed against tomorrow must still be repaid.
{elder} stamps a seal on your hand and says that every contract is a small formation, and that you should read its array before signing.
{elder} teaches that a loss admitted early is cheaper than a profit hidden late; {topic} rewards honest hands.
{elder} lets the abacus rest and speaks for an hour on knowing what a thing is worth to the one who wants it.
